item.title: NEW: NPM Package 'tensorlake' Hit by Self-Propagating Supply Chain Worm
item.description:
Headline: NPM Package 'tensorlake' Hit by Self-Propagating Supply Chain Worm

Summary:
The 'tensorlake' NPM package, a TypeScript SDK for AI applications, was compromised with a self-propagating worm from the 'Shai-Hulud' family. The malicious version, 0.5.144, was published to the NPM registry and contained obfuscated malware designed to harvest a wide array of credentials from developer environments, including secrets from CI/CD pipelines, AWS, Kubernetes, and cryptocurrency wallets. The worm uses the stolen credentials to automatically republish compromised versions of other packages associated with the victim's account, furthering the supply chain attack. The malware uses an Ethereum smart contract for resilient command-and-control.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Malware, Threat Actor

Meta Description: A supply chain attack compromised the 'tensorlake' NPM package with a self-propagating worm that steals developer credentials and secrets from CI/CD pipelines.

item.title: NEW: Ransomware Attack Cripples Japanese Cloud Provider IDCF Cloud
item.description:
Headline: Ransomware Attack Cripples Japanese Cloud Provider IDCF Cloud

Summary:
IDC Frontier, a major Japanese cloud provider and SoftBank subsidiary, has suffered a significant ransomware attack impacting its IDCF Cloud service. The attack, which began on October 7, 2026, targeted the 'East Japan Region 1' data center, causing a widespread outage. The company was forced to shut down affected systems to contain the threat, impacting 495 corporate and local government clients. The attackers claimed to have encrypted 3.6 PB of data across 225 databases in just seven minutes. IDC Frontier has disabled customer access to management consoles while it investigates the intrusion.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Cyberattack, Cloud Security

Meta Description: Japanese cloud provider IDC Frontier suffered a major ransomware attack on its IDCF Cloud service, causing widespread outages for 495 corporate and government clients.

item.title: NEW: APT Uses AI and QR Codes in Phishing Attack on Taiwan Researchers
item.description:
Headline: APT Uses AI and QR Codes in Phishing Attack on Taiwan Researchers

Summary:
An unidentified Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group is conducting a sophisticated spear-phishing campaign against Taiwanese research organizations. According to Cisco Talos, the attackers are using what appears to be AI-generated content to create convincing email lures impersonating academic institutions. The campaign also employs QR code phishing ('quishing') and an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing framework to intercept credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA). The AitM kit impersonates Google login pages and uses a hybrid HTTP/WebSocket architecture to capture credentials and MFA tokens in real-time.

Severity: High

Categories: Phishing, Threat Actor, Data Breach

Meta Description: An APT group is using AI-generated content, QR codes, and an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) framework to bypass MFA in a phishing campaign against Taiwan.

Article Slug: apt-uses-ai-and-qr-codes-in-phishing-campaign-against-taiwan

item.title: NEW: Phishing Attacks Abusing Legitimate RMM Tools Surge by 475%
item.description:
Headline: Phishing Attacks Abusing Legitimate RMM Tools Surge by 475%

Summary:
Phishing campaigns abusing legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools have increased by 475% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to all of 2025. According to Fortra, these attacks primarily target North American financial institutions. Attackers use social engineering to trick victims into granting remote access via tools like ScreenConnect and AnyDesk. A separate campaign detailed by Huntress shows attackers using Microsoft Power BI domains to host lures that lead to the download of a rogue ScreenConnect installer, a technique that helps evade security filters.

Severity: High

Categories: Phishing, Cyberattack, Malware

Meta Description: Phishing attacks that abuse legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools have surged by 475%, with attackers targeting financial institutions.

item.title: NEW: North Korean Hackers Use Public Blockchain for Covert C2 Channel
item.description:
Headline: North Korean Hackers Use Public Blockchain for Covert C2 Channel

Summary:
The North Korea-affiliated threat group Alluring Pisces (also known as Sapphire Sleet) is using a public blockchain for its command-and-control (C2) communications in cloud supply chain attacks. According to research from Unit 42, this novel technique makes the C2 infrastructure highly resilient and nearly impossible to take down. The group employs this method in campaigns like 'ChainDrop' and 'PolinRider,' which poison open-source packages on npm, Go, and Packagist to steal cloud credentials from developer environments and CI/CD pipelines.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Threat Actor, Supply Chain Attack, Cloud Security

Meta Description: The North Korean hacking group Alluring Pisces is using public blockchains for command-and-control (C2) in cloud supply chain attacks, making them highly resilient.

item.title: NEW: Owner of Ransomware Recovery Firm Charged with Wire Fraud
item.description:
Headline: Owner of Ransomware Recovery Firm Charged with Wire Fraud

Summary:
Zohar Pinhasi, the owner of ransomware recovery firm MonsterCloud, has been indicted by the U.S. Department of Justice on wire fraud charges. Pinhasi is accused of deceiving clients by falsely claiming his company could decrypt their data using proprietary technology without paying a ransom. The indictment alleges that, in reality, MonsterCloud would secretly negotiate with and pay the ransomware attackers to obtain the decryption key, then charge the victims for their 'decryption services' while concealing the ransom payment.

Severity: Informational

Categories: Policy and Compliance, Ransomware, Regulatory

Meta Description: The U.S. Department of Justice has charged Zohar Pinhasi, owner of ransomware recovery firm MonsterCloud, with wire fraud for allegedly paying ransoms in secret.

item.title: NEW: FBI: China-Linked Hackers Gave Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
item.description:
Headline: FBI: China-Linked Hackers Gave Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails

Summary:
An international advisory led by the FBI reveals that hackers linked to the sanctioned Chinese company Integrity Technology Group operated a web portal to provide third-party access to stolen email content. The campaign, active since at least January 2021, targeted a wide range of sectors globally, including government, healthcare, and critical manufacturing in the U.S., Southeast Asia, and Africa. The attackers used vulnerability scanning, password guessing, and specialized tools to compromise Microsoft 365 and Exchange accounts and exfiltrate entire mailboxes.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Data Breach, Cyberattack

Meta Description: An FBI-led advisory reveals that China-linked hackers operated a web portal to provide third-party access to emails stolen from Microsoft 365 and Exchange.

item.title: NEW: New 'Wazza' Phishkit Uses Advanced Evasion to Target Global Orgs
item.description:
Headline: New 'Wazza' Phishkit Uses Advanced Evasion to Target Global Orgs

Summary:
A new and sophisticated phishing kit dubbed 'Wazza' is targeting banking, manufacturing, and government organizations in the US, Europe, and Australia. According to researchers at ANY.RUN, the kit uses a multi-stage routing chain to filter out security scanners, sandboxes, and other automated traffic. This ensures the final phishing page, typically an Adobe-themed lure for Device Code phishing, is only delivered to intended human victims. This advanced evasion complicates detection and increases the workload for security analysts.

Severity: Medium

Categories: Phishing, Malware

Meta Description: The 'Wazza' phishing kit is targeting global organizations with advanced evasion techniques, using a multi-stage routing chain to filter out security scanners.
